epithet: The surah that turned his hair grey
lede: Abū Bakr said: Messenger of Allah, you have gone grey. He ﷺ said: “Hūd and its sisters have turned me grey.” Six peoples pass through it, each warned by one of their own and each destroyed — and then, to the man hearing it, one command: stand firm, as you have been commanded.

names.name: Hūd
names.note: After the prophet sent to ʿĀd, whose story it tells (11:50–60) — and whose name is repeated in it more than in any other surah.

revelation.detail: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥah relates from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is Makkan, all of it, and so said al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, Mujāhid, Jābir ibn Zayd and Qatādah. One report from Ibn ʿAbbās, and one from Qatādah, except a single ayah — “Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day” (11:114) — on account of the man in Madinah about whom it is related. The traditional order places it fifty-second, between Yūnus and Yūsuf: the last, hardest years in Makkah.

evidence.quote: رَوى ابْنُ أبِي طَلْحَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها، وبِهِ قالَ الحَسَنُ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وجابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، وقَتادَةُ
قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَدْ شِبْتَ؟ قَالَ: " شَيَّبَتْنِي هُودٌ، وَالْوَاقِعَةُ، وَالْمُرْسَلَاتُ، وَعَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ، وَإِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ

setting: It follows Yūnus in the muṣḥaf and in the order of revelation, and tells some of the same histories; but the tone has changed. Yūnus appealed. Hūd warns. In Yūnus one people believes at the last moment and is spared. Here there are six, and not one of them is.

The stories run in the order of time, and each messenger is given his own voice. Nūḥ, at the greatest length: nine hundred and fifty years reduced to a few exchanges — “I do not ask you for wealth; I shall not drive away those who believe” — then the building of the ship while the chiefs walk past laughing, the oven gushing, the waves like mountains, and a father calling to his son across the water: “My son, come aboard with us.” — “I shall take refuge on a mountain.” Then the word that ends it: “O earth, swallow your water; O sky, withhold.” And when Nūḥ pleads for the boy afterwards: “He is not of your family.”

Hūd, alone before ʿĀd: “I call Allah to witness, and you bear witness, that I am free of what you associate. So plot against me, all of you together, and give me no respite. I have put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord.” Ṣāliḥ and the she-camel. The angels who come to Ibrāhīm as guests, and laugh with his wife over the news of a son, on their way to the towns of Lūṭ. Lūṭ himself, wishing he had some strong support to lean on. Shuʿayb, to whom his people say, “Does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worshipped, or stop doing what we like with our own wealth?” — and who answers with a sentence that reformers have quoted ever since: “I want only to set things right, as far as I am able; and my success is only through Allah.”

Then the surah turns to the Prophet ﷺ and tells him what it was all for. “All that We relate to you of the news of the messengers is that by which We make your heart firm.” And it lays on him the charge that, Ibn ʿAbbās said, was the heaviest ayah ever sent down to him: “So stand firm as you have been commanded — you, and those who have turned with you — and do not transgress.” With it come three more: do not lean towards those who do wrong; keep up the prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night; and be patient.

occasions.title: “Good deeds drive away evil deeds”
occasions.text: A man kissed a woman, and came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him of it. Then there was sent down to him: “Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night; good deeds drive away evil deeds.” The man said: “Is this for me alone?” He said: “For whoever of my community acts on it.”
occasions.source: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: al-Bukhārī (4687) and Muslim (2763).

aim: To set out the way of the messengers in facing those of their people who denied them.
themes: The Book whose ayat are perfected
Stories that make the heart firm

outline.title: A Book made firm, then set out
outline.summary: Alif Lām Rā. A Book whose ayat are perfected, then set out in detail, from One who is Wise, Aware: that you worship none but Allah. Seek your Lord’s forgiveness, then turn to Him. There is no creature on the earth but its provision is upon Allah. He created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water. Perhaps you would leave out part of what is revealed to you. Do they say he invented it? Then bring ten surahs like it. The two parties are like the blind and deaf, and the seeing and hearing.

outline.title: Nūḥ
outline.summary: We sent Nūḥ to his people: “I am to you a clear warner.” The chiefs said: “We see that none follow you but the lowest of us.” — “I shall not drive away those who believe.” Build the ship under Our eyes. When Our command came and the oven gushed: load upon it of every kind a pair. It sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Nūḥ called to his son. “O earth, swallow your water; O sky, withhold.” — “My Lord, my son is of my family.” — “Nūḥ, he is not of your family.”

outline.title: Hūd and Ṣāliḥ
outline.summary: To ʿĀd, their brother Hūd: “My people, ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him; He will send the sky upon you in abundance and add strength to your strength.” — “I have put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but He holds it by the forelock.” To Thamūd, their brother Ṣāliḥ: “He brought you forth from the earth and settled you in it.” They hamstrung her; he said: “Enjoy yourselves in your homes three days.”

outline.title: The guests of Ibrāhīm, and Lūṭ
outline.summary: Our messengers came to Ibrāhīm with good news. He brought a roasted calf; when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he felt a fear of them. His wife stood by and laughed, and We gave her good news of Isḥāq, and after Isḥāq, Yaʿqūb. Ibrāhīm was forbearing, tender-hearted, ever turning to Allah. When Our messengers came to Lūṭ he was distressed for them: “Would that I had power against you, or could lean on some strong support.” — “Their appointed time is the morning. Is the morning not near?”

outline.title: Shuʿayb, and Mūsā
outline.summary: To Madyan, their brother Shuʿayb: “Do not give short measure and weight.” — “Shuʿayb, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worshipped?” — “I do not wish to do, behind your backs, what I forbid you. I want only to set things right, as far as I am able; and my success is only through Allah” (11:88). — “Were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you.” And We sent Mūsā to Pharaoh, who will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them down into the Fire.

outline.title: What it means
outline.summary: That is of the news of the towns, which We relate to you; some of them stand, and some are mown down. We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. Such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong. That is a Day to which mankind will be gathered: some of them wretched, and some happy. As for the wretched, they are in the Fire; as for the happy, they are in the Garden — a gift never cut off.

outline.title: Stand firm
outline.summary: So stand firm as you have been commanded, you and those who have turned with you, and do not transgress. Do not lean towards those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you. Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night; good deeds drive away evil deeds. Be patient. Had your Lord willed, He would have made mankind one community. All that We relate to you of the news of the messengers is that by which We make your heart firm. To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth; so worship Him and rely on Him.

keyAyah.why: The command that all its stories lead to. Ibn ʿAbbās said that no ayah was sent down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ harder or heavier upon him than this.

virtues.text: Abū Bakr said: “Messenger of Allah, you have gone grey.” He said: “Hūd, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn and Idhā l-shamsu kuwwirat have turned me grey.”
virtues.arabic: شَيَّبَتْنِي هُودٌ وَالْوَاقِعَةُ وَالْمُرْسَلاَتُ وَعَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ وَإِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ

evidence.quote: قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ مَا نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ آيَةٌ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَلَا أَشَقُّ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ عَلَيْهِ، وَلِذَلِكَ قَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ حِينَ قَالُوا لَهُ: لَقَدْ أَسْرَعَ إِلَيْكَ الشَّيْبُ! فَقَالَ: "شَيَّبَتْنِي هُودٌ وَأَخَوَاتُهَا

virtues.text: “Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer — until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape.” Then he recited: “Such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong. His seizure is painful, severe.”
virtues.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَيُمْلِي لِلظَّالِمِ حَتَّى إِذَا أَخَذَهُ لَمْ يُفْلِتْهُ

virtues.text: “Allah, mighty and majestic, has said: ‘Spend, and I shall spend on you.’ The Hand of Allah is full; no spending diminishes it, pouring forth night and day. Have you seen what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? It has not lessened what is in His Hand. And His Throne was upon the water; and in His Hand is the balance: He lowers and He raises.”

virtuesNote: Al-Qurṭubī cites from al-Dārimī a report, through Kaʿb, “Recite Sūrat Hūd on Fridays.” It is a mursal report — the link to the Prophet ﷺ is missing — and is not relied on.
before: Yūnus ended: “be patient until Allah judges.” Hūd shows what that judgement looked like, six times over.
after: Hūd ends by saying that the stories of the messengers are told to make the Prophet’s heart firm. Yūsuf opens: “We relate to you the best of stories” — and tells one, from beginning to end.
